title: Bodo Traditional Cuisine & Indigenous Gastronomy
description: Culinary traditions emphasizing indigenous fermentation, wild medicinal greens, alkali ash water, and zero-oil cooking techniques.

dishes.name: Napham (नाफाम)
dishes.ingredients: Small indigenous river fish, powdered taro stem, dried wild herbs.
dishes.preparation: Fish is cleaned, pounded with seasoned dried taro and spices, sealed air-tight inside bamboo internodes for several months to mature into a rich umami paste.

dishes.name: Oma jwng narjwi (अमा जों नारजै)
dishes.ingredients: Pork, sun-dried jute leaves (narjwi), green chilies, ginger-garlic.
dishes.preparation: Pork pieces are simmered with dry bitter jute leaves until a savory, mildly bitter, aromatic gravy forms, famous for cooling the body in humid summers.

dishes.name: Kharwi / Gwka (खारवि / गोखा)
dishes.ingredients: Plantain tree peel ash water (Kharwi), seasonal vegetables, small fish.
dishes.preparation: Water filtered through the ash of sun-dried banana peels produces a golden alkaline liquid with distinct medicinal properties, cooked with bitter vegetables or wild spinach.

dishes.name: Sobai jwng oma (सबाय जों अमा)
dishes.ingredients: Black gram (sobai), pork or duck meat, indigenous spices.
dishes.preparation: Black lentils slow-cooked with fresh pork over wood fire into a thick hearty stew, ubiquitous during Bwisagu and wedding feasts.

dishes.name: Mwitha jwng dao (मैथा जों दाव)
dishes.ingredients: Local country chicken, sour roselle leaves (mwitha).
dishes.preparation: Country chicken cooked with young sour roselle leaves, creating a bright tangy broth aiding digestion.

dishes.name: Jou & Amaw (जौ आरो आमाव)
dishes.ingredients: Rice, indigenous medicinal herbs (Emao starter cakes).
dishes.preparation: Steamed glutinous rice mixed with wild medicinal starter cakes and fermented in earthen pots into two forms: Jou Gwran (potent spirit) and Jou Gisi (sweet refreshing beer).
